why: Petrol, diesel and LPG pink slips

qa.q: How much is a pink slip?
qa.also: pink slip cost, price, fee, how much, rego check price, safety check cost, e-safety, esafety
qa.a: The NSW Government sets the most any station can charge for a car: $52 for a pink slip, from 1 July 2026. If it doesn't pass and is fixed and checked again here within 14 days, there's no second inspection fee.

qa.q: How much is a blue slip?
qa.also: blue slip cost, price, fee, AUVIS, identity check cost
qa.a: The most a station can charge for a blue slip on a car is $82, set by the NSW Government from 1 July 2026.

qa.also: pink slip, rego check, safety check, esafety, inspection, renew rego, do I need a pink slip
qa.a: A pink slip is the safety check most light vehicles need to renew their rego once they're more than five years old, counted from the compliance plate date. It checks things like tyres, brakes, steering and suspension, lights, windscreen and wipers, seatbelts, body and rust, and the exhaust. The report is valid for six months.

qa.q: Do I need a blue slip?
qa.also: blue slip, unregistered, interstate car, expired rego, no plates, written off, register a car in NSW, identity check
qa.a: You need a blue slip, a safety and identity check, when the rego ran out more than three months ago, the vehicle comes from interstate or overseas, it has no plates, or it's a written-off vehicle being registered again. The report is valid for 42 days.

qa.q: Does a new car need a pink slip?
qa.also: under 5 years, new car rego, 3 year old car, no inspection
qa.a: Cars up to five years old usually renew their rego without an inspection. Your renewal notice says whether you need one. A logbook service is still worth booking.

qa.q: Do you do pink slips for LPG and diesel cars?
qa.also: lpg, gas car, diesel, petrol, dual fuel
qa.a: We do pink slips for petrol, diesel and LPG vehicles.

qa.q: What happens if my car fails the pink slip?
qa.also: fail, failed, didn't pass, recheck, re-inspection, fix and recheck
qa.a: We'll tell you what failed. It needs to be fixed before it can pass. If it's fixed and checked again here within 14 days, there's no second inspection fee, and we can do the repairs in the workshop.

qa.also: hours, open, opening times, when are you open, close, closing time, today, weekdays
qa.a: Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm, Saturday 9am to 2pm. We're closed on Sundays.

qa.also: saturday, weekend
qa.a: Saturday 9am to 2pm.

qa.also: sunday
qa.a: No, we're closed on Sundays. We're open Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to 2pm.

qa.a: Call the workshop on (02) 8798 5715, or Balli on his mobile, 0433 597 181. Tell us the make and model and what the car is doing, and we'll find a time.

qa.also: services, what do you do, work, mechanic, repairs, offer
qa.a: All mechanical repairs (engine, brakes, steering, suspension and defect clearances), pink slips for petrol, diesel and LPG vehicles, blue slips, logbook servicing, air con regas and repairs, tyres and batteries.

qa.also: logbook, service, car service, scheduled service, oil change, service book
qa.a: We service cars to their logbook schedule. Bring your service book with you and tell us the kilometres when you call.

qa.q: Can you fix my air con?
qa.also: air con, aircon, air conditioning, regas, not cold, blowing warm, ac
qa.a: We do air con regas, repairs and servicing for air con that has stopped blowing cold.

qa.also: tyres, tires, new tyres, flat tyre, tread
qa.a: We do tyres, for when yours are worn, damaged or keep losing air.

qa.also: battery, flat battery, won't start, car won't start, jump start
qa.a: We do batteries. If the car is slow to start or won't start at all, the battery is the first thing to check.

qa.also: brakes, squealing, grinding, pads, rotors, brake noise, suspension, steering
qa.a: Brakes, steering and suspension are part of our mechanical repairs. Call and tell us what the car is doing.

qa.q: What does the warning light on my dash mean?
qa.also: warning light, dash light, check engine light, engine light, battery light, oil light, abs light, light on
qa.a: Tap the light you can see in the warning lights section for what it usually means and whether to keep driving. As a rule of thumb, red usually means stop when it's safe, and amber means get it checked soon.
